items.name: assertSafePath path traversal defense
items.summary: Resolves user-supplied paths against an allowed root, rejects null bytes and traversals — closes Cortex CRITICAL Flaw #51 (unsandboxed source) and #74 (read_entity path injection)
items.counter_case: Cortex's source tool serves only .knowledge/ — a path-allow-list might be simpler than full canonicalization; but canonicalization is more robust if roots ever expand.

items.name: assertString type-confusion prevention
items.summary: Rejects array parameters (?x=a&x=b) before any string operation — closes CodeQL js/type-confusion-through-parameter-tampering, relevant to Cortex's MCP tool parameter handling
items.counter_case: MCP parameters arrive as typed JSON, not HTTP query strings — this is most relevant only if Cortex adds HTTP routes (Phase 22).

items.name: Schema version guard for incremental state
items.summary: INCREMENTAL_SCHEMA_VERSION constant bumped on breaking change forces full rebuild — directly closes Flaw #63 (state.json version never checked)
items.counter_case: Cortex's state.json is simpler than GitNexus's registry; schema changes are infrequent — but the guard is near-zero effort and the payoff is high.

items.name: Doctor capabilities fingerprint
items.summary: getRuntimeFingerprint() + getRuntimeCapabilities() reports OS/Node/DB/ONNX, graph store, FTS, vector, semantic mode — closes Flaw #98 (no cortex doctor)
items.counter_case: Phase 0.7 already plans cortex doctor; GitNexus's version adds ONNX/DB capability probing that Cortex doesn't need until Phase 0.14.

items.name: RRF K=60 hybrid search + BM25 top-3 aggregation
items.summary: RRF (1/(K+rank+1), K=60) merges BM25 + semantic ranks without score normalization; top-3 node aggregation per file prevents test-file score inflation — closes Flaw #26 (ranks by substring, not relevance)
items.counter_case: Cortex's Phase 0.9 plans IDF+BFS ranking already; RRF requires both FTS and vector indexes operational — adds complexity without full embedding support.

items.name: Crash-recovery dirty flag (incrementalInProgress)
items.summary: incrementalInProgress written to meta.json BEFORE destructive mutation, cleared only on success — next run sees the flag and forces full rebuild, closes Flaw #120 (partial manifest overwrite)
items.counter_case: Cortex doesn't yet have an incremental update mode — this is a Phase 33.6 concern, not immediately needed.

items.name: Content-addressed incremental reindex fileHashes map
items.summary: fileHashes: Record<string,string> maps repo-relative paths to SHA-256 content hashes; next run diffs hashes, rewrites only changed-file rows — prevents full re-extract of unchanged files
items.counter_case: Cortex ingests LLM-synthesized knowledge, not just parse output — content hash only answers 'did the source change', not 'did the synthesis change'; needs a separate knowledge hash.

items.name: SHA1 embedding version hash (EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION)
items.summary: EMBEDDING_TEXT_VERSION prefix + SHA1(text) stored per node; incremental runs skip re-embed when hash unchanged; bump version to invalidate all embeddings on template change
items.counter_case: Only needed once Phase 0.14 embeddings ship; premature if embeddings aren't incrementally generated yet.

items.name: Cross-platform path canonicalization (realpathSync.native)
items.summary: realpathSync.native() resolves symlinks + Windows 8.3 short-name forms to canonical long paths; graceful fallback to path.resolve() for non-existent paths — prevents entity ID mismatch across paths to same file
items.counter_case: Cortex runs on the developer's machine only; symlink aliasing is less common in single-user local environments — but macOS /var→/private/var and Windows runner short names affect CI.

items.name: Adaptive concurrency reduction on LLM 429
items.summary: When LLM returns 429, reduce activeConcurrency by 1 and re-queue the failed item with 5s backoff — automatically rights the concurrency without requiring manual tuning
items.counter_case: Cortex doesn't run concurrent LLM calls today (single synthesis path); only relevant once Phase 2 bulk synthesis or wiki generation ships.

items.name: Dual-framing MCP transport + 10 MB buffer cap
items.summary: Auto-detects Content-Length vs newline-delimited JSON framing on first byte; 10 MB buffer cap discards oversized input before allocating; iterative loop (not recursive) prevents stack overflow on malformed input
items.counter_case: Cortex's MCP is stdio-only and the SDK handles framing — this pattern is redundant if using @modelcontextprotocol/sdk's default transport. Only needed for a custom transport layer.

items.name: IPv6 rate limiting normalization to /56 subnet
items.summary: ipKeyGenerator normalizes IPv6 addresses to /56 subnet prefix before rate-limit keying — prevents per-address IPv6 bypass with 2^72 addresses per /56 network
items.counter_case: Only relevant when Phase 22 Central Knowledge Server ships; premature for local-only Cortex.

items.name: Noisy contract filter (health-check and param-only paths)
items.summary: Configurable exclude_links_paths (/health, /ready) + exclude_links_param_only_paths removes N×M false cross-repo dependencies from infrastructure health-check routes
items.counter_case: Phase 11.5 contract registry is future; may not need this filter if Cortex only indexes higher-level semantic contracts rather than HTTP routes.

items.name: Retry with full-jitter exponential backoff + Retry-After honor
items.summary: delay = random() × min(cap, base × 2^attempt); if server sends Retry-After header, uses min(afterMs, capDelayMs) — honors server throttle signals without blindly trusting them
items.counter_case: Cortex's LLM calls use Claude's SDK which may already handle retries; would need to verify SDK behavior before adding a second layer.

items.name: Deadline-driven fanout with AbortController racing
items.summary: Cross-repo impact fans out to N neighbors each raced against remainingMs = deadline - Date.now(); timed-out neighbors appended to truncatedRepos list rather than hanging the response
items.counter_case: Phase 11.5 groups are future; also, Cortex's local-first constraint limits cross-repo fanout to local repos (no network hops), making hung calls less likely.

items.name: Smart section preservation (<!-- gitnexus:keep -->)
items.summary: When <!-- gitnexus:keep --> marker is present, analyze only updates the stats line (symbol counts) — allows teams to maintain a custom AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md layout that survives re-indexing
items.counter_case: Cortex's managed CLAUDE.md (Phase 10.4) is future; this pattern shines in teams with divergent CLAUDE.md customizations — single-dev Cortex installs rarely need it.

items.name: MCP Tool Annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint)
items.summary: ToolAnnotations on every MCP tool signals to clients which tools are read-only vs destructive vs idempotent — clients auto-partition and avoid unnecessary confirmation prompts for read-only calls
items.counter_case: MCP SDK may or may not surface annotations to agents; benefit depends on client capability — Cursor and Claude Code may not act on these hints yet.

items.name: Embedding metadata text header (label + path + export + description)
items.summary: Prepend structured header (Label: Name / Repo: / Path: / Export: / Description: truncated) before code body — structural context improves embedding discriminability across same-named symbols in different files
items.counter_case: Token overhead of header reduces body context in fixed-size embedding windows; may hurt small models on large symbols.

items.name: MCP stray-stdout sentinel (AsyncLocalStorage tagging)
items.summary: AsyncLocalStorage tags legitimate MCP writes; stray writes (from logs, deps) redirected to stderr with [mcp:stdout-redirect] prefix, truncated to 200 bytes, rate-limited to 10 per process — prevents hung handshakes
items.counter_case: Only needed if Cortex uses dependencies that write to stdout; the MCP SDK itself is clean — this adds complexity for a hypothetical problem.

items.name: Three-tier contract lookup index for O(1) resolution
items.summary: Built-once in-memory index: tier-1 repo+role+symbolUid, tier-2 repo+role+filePath+symbolName, tier-3 repo+role+filePath → eliminates N+1 DB round-trips per cross-link resolution
items.counter_case: Cortex's cross-repo is Phase 11.5 future; this optimization is premature until there are enough contract rows to matter.

items.name: Sibling-clone staleness detection
items.summary: checkCwdMatch() finds registered repos with same remoteUrl at different on-disk path; warns that sibling clone's HEAD differs from indexed commit — prevents silent stale answers when switching worktrees
items.counter_case: Cortex tracks projectRoot explicitly; users working in a second clone should re-run cortex analyze — the warning is helpful but not critical for single-developer local use.

items.name: Circuit breaker with half-open probe + recordNeutral()
items.summary: recordNeutral() releases half-open probe permit without counting as success or failure — prevents TimeoutError from permanently parking the breaker in half-open; thundering-herd prevention via single probe in-flight
items.counter_case: Cortex's LLM calls are sequential (not concurrent) and short-lived — a circuit breaker adds complexity for a scenario (flapping LLM backend) that Cortex's local-first principle avoids.

items.name: LadybugDB persistent graph DB (vs knowledge-as-derived-data)
items.summary: GitNexus's DB-backed graph enables native FTS, vector indexes, and Cypher queries — Cortex's JSON-file approach is simpler and portable but lacks these capabilities
items.steel_man: DB-backed storage with native FTS and vector indexes removes the need to implement BM25 and ANN search from scratch; at scale (>50k nodes) it's clearly superior to JSON scanning.

items.name: Web UI for graph exploration (vs local-first)
items.summary: GitNexus's browser UI enables non-developer graph exploration without any local setup — Cortex's .knowledge/ wiki + Obsidian is simpler for developer workflows
items.steel_man: Browser-based viewer (HTML with embedded JSON) has zero install friction and works for non-technical stakeholders; Cortex's Phase 8 visual graph is entirely local.

items.name: LadybugDB WAL checkpoint threshold control
items.principle_violated: knowledge-as-derived-data / local-first — Cortex uses JSON, not a WAL DB
items.summary: 64 MiB default WAL threshold reduces checkpoint churn under heavy writes — inapplicable until Cortex adopts a WAL-capable DB backend (Phase 3.1+)

items.name: COBOL support via regex (no tree-sitter)
items.principle_violated: niche — not in Cortex's target languages list
items.summary: COBOL pipeline phase uses regex extractors (no tree-sitter grammar available) — interesting approach but COBOL is not in Cortex's Phase 0.13 language priorities

items.name: LLM-driven wiki generation (4-phase pipeline)

items.summary: GitNexus generates module wikis via LLM (1 grouping call + N module calls + 1 overview call) — Cortex wiki (Phase 8.2) should generate from graph structure without LLM calls

items.name: CI parity workflow (dual-path simultaneous execution)
items.principle_violated: niche — specific to GitNexus's two-resolution-path migration
items.summary: Runs both legacy Call-Resolution DAG and new Scope-Resolution pipeline on every PR — migration-specific pattern for a codebase that can't break existing language support mid-migration

items.name: Scarf analytics in npm package

items.name: FTS query string interpolation risk
items.pattern: CALL QUERY_FTS_INDEX template-interpolates table/index names (trusted) but queries user input via $query parameter — the original version interpolated the query string directly, causing FTS injection (backslash escape exploit)
items.why_target_chose_it: FTS5 table and index names are compile-time constants, so the dev initially treated the entire query as a format string; user input was added later without re-evaluating the injection surface.
items.cortex_lesson: Any FTS or Cypher query builder in Cortex (Phase 0.9) must separate compile-time schema identifiers (safe to interpolate) from runtime user input (must be parameterized). Never interpolate search terms.

items.name: MCP buffer memory allocation before Content-Length validation
items.source: gitnexus/CHANGELOG.md:88-90 — v1.3.10 fix; now fixed in compatible-stdio-transport.ts:64-68
items.pattern: The original transport allocated the read buffer to Content-Length size BEFORE checking if it exceeded MAX_BUFFER_SIZE — a malicious client could trigger OOM by sending Content-Length: 99999999999
items.why_target_chose_it: Transport code was ported from the MCP SDK reference implementation which didn't have the adversarial-input assumption.
items.cortex_lesson: Any Cortex MCP or HTTP transport that reads a Content-Length header MUST validate the value against a cap BEFORE allocating any buffer. Check first, allocate second.

items.name: Should Cortex adopt a DB connection pool when Phase 3.x ships?
items.question: When Cortex moves to a graph DB backend (Phase 3.1), should it adopt GitNexus's LRU connection pool pattern (MAX_POOL_SIZE=5, IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=5min, pool-close listeners for cache invalidation)?
alternatives: A: Single shared connection per process (simple, sufficient for local-only single-writer)
B: Per-request connection with open/close overhead (safe but slow for MCP server under load)
C: LRU pool as GitNexus does (best throughput, needed only if MCP concurrency is observed)

items.name: Should Cortex run shadow-mode parity tests during Phase 33.5 pipeline migration?
items.question: Phase 33.5 introduces a two-stage ingestion pipeline replacing the existing single-pass. Should Cortex run both pipelines simultaneously in CI (as GitNexus does for its legacy DAG → scope-resolver migration) and fail on divergence?
alternatives: A: Shadow CI parity (expensive but catches regressions; GitNexus approach)
B: Snapshot-based regression tests (compare output on a fixed fixture corpus)
C: Feature flag per language with manual validation (lower safety, faster migration)
